chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died before having intercourse with his wife, he said: If he had assigned a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of it, and she inherits him. And if he had not assigned a dower for her, then there is no dower for her, and he inherits her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's dower and inheritance if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a wife in the 'partial marriage' phase, where the marriage contract is valid but consummation has not occurred. It establishes that she is entitled to half the dower (Mahr) and full inheritance rights, reflecting the Shia juristic consensus that the marriage bond is fully effective for inheritance purposes even without physical union. This ruling underscores the principle that the husband's death triggers the wife's inheritance share regardless of consummation, provided the contract was valid.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who died before having gone to bed with his wife. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the dower was assigned for her, so for her is the half (of it), and she would inherit him. And if a dower was not assigned to her, so there is no dower for her, and he would inherit her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ‘Uthman from ibn abu Ya’fur who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who dies before going to bed with his wife. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If mahr (dower) was assigned for her, she receives one-half as well as her share of inheritance but if mahr (dower) was not assigned she does not have any mahr (dower) but inherits from the legacy.’”
